plan: With a private value of $40, I want to maximize potential profit. In a sealed bid ascending auction, I need to strategically choose an exit price. My optimal strategy is to bid slightly below my true value, around $39-$39.50. This allows me to potentially win if others bid lower, while protecting some profit margin. I'll aim to exit just above the second-highest sealed bid to minimize my payment while maximizing my chances of winning.

In a single round with a private value of $13, I want to maximize potential profit. My strategy will be to bid slightly below my true value to create a buffer. Since the second-highest sealed bid determines the final price, I'll aim to bid around $11-12. This gives me a chance to win if others bid higher, while protecting some potential profit margin. The key is balancing winning probability with profit preservation.

In a single round with independent value draw, I want to maximize expected profit. My value is $17. In Stage 2, I'll exit when the clock price approaches my sealed bid. My optimal strategy is to bid slightly below my true value to create a buffer. Since the winner pays the second-highest sealed bid, I'll bid around $16 to potentially win while preserving some profit margin if I win.
